A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MixLoRA-DSI. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments on NQ320k, MSMARCO and LongEval, alongside component ablations, hyperparameter studies and routing analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports document-identifier comparisons and an auxiliary-loss ablation.

M1.justification: The OOD expansion rule, cosine router, two-term auxiliary loss, RQ masking, slow learning and KL regularization remain unchanged. Newly evaluated identifier and loss variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same dynamic-retrieval tasks on NQ320k, MSMARCO and LongEval. LongEval already appears in v1 Appendix B.3 and moves to v2 Appendix B.5; the new ablations use existing datasets.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 adds atomic and PQ-based identifiers as evaluated alternatives to RQ-based identifiers within MixLoRA-DSI-PT. Comparator membership in the existing benchmark comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations compare identifier configurations, include FAISS exact-search diagnostics, and report separate on/off controls for the auxiliary-loss terms. Existing splits, training budgets, model sizes and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices B.1 and B.3 add targeted analyses of identifier choice and the contributions of individual router-loss terms. Existing component, hyperparameter, routing and OOD analyses are retained. The new loss-ablation reporting has inconsistencies discussed in the overall assessment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in v1's twelve tables are retained. New Table 9 reports AP Recall@10 of 44.4, 3.4 and 53.2 for atomic, PQ and RQ identifiers, respectively, plus vocabulary footprints. v2 also adds exact-search findings and loss-specific entries in Table 13, although the latter duplicate four Table 4 rows under different control labels.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, loss formulas, energy criterion and appendix derivations remain substantively unchanged. Equation 7 changes query-set notation, and the new masking example illustrates the existing rule without adding a formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same novelty, sublinear-growth, efficiency and forgetting claims. One introductory 'first to view' phrase is removed, but the explicit first OOD-driven expansion-framework contribution remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of semantic-identifier compatibility, PQ quality, atomic-identifier memory costs and the roles of individual loss terms. Section 4.2 now describes BM25's degradation as performance drift. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: A new page-one footnote supplies a repository link for the authors' code; v1 provided only third-party implementation links. Appendix E retains the existing hardware, optimizer, hyperparameters and training details.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Nogueira et al. (2019) docT5query reference and expands discussion of PQ and atomic identifiers in relation to earlier retrieval methods. The dedicated related-work section and broader positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the pseudo-query explanation, connects the expansion procedure more explicitly to Figure 2, and adds a worked masking example. It also adds author emails, acknowledgments and appendix subsections while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn and enlarged with revised annotations. Two appendix tables are added, existing displays are reflowed or renumbered, and several metric headings expand R@10/M@10 to Recall@10/MRR@10.

improvement.justification: Clearer explanations, a code-access link and the identifier comparison offer benefits. However, new Table 13 reproduces Table 4 rows 1, 2, 3 and 6 under different loss controls. Appendix B.3's claim that either single term worsens forgetting conflicts with the second-term-only row, and its MSMARCO discussion lacks separately reported supporting results. With the core evidence unchanged, these unresolved reporting problems prevent a reliable judgment of net improvement.
